The authors aim for balance over hype. A timely guide for biology teachers facing the AI question.
openalex-w7204260448: Energy drinks promise focus but may frazzle the brain. This integrative review studies what the science says about these beverages' effects on the central nervous system. The authors screened Portuguese and English research from 2021 to mid-2025. A timely review of the can behind the buzz.
openalex-w7128707048: Robots are entering the chest surgeon's toolkit. This paper reports Juntendo University's experience with robot-assisted lung cancer surgery since 2017: safety and benefits. The authors tracked the program's growth past 15 percent of cases. A surgical report from the robotic frontier.
openalex-w7214311248: Undoing an ileostomy can leave a hernia where the stoma was. This study of 194 patients hunted risk factors for these hernias, with focus on what thread closed the muscle layer. The team counted how often they struck. A surgery study of closing bellies cleanly.
arxiv-2606-16148: This chip paper has a twin: the AIA speed story. Its tricks: a smart way to draw dice-roll numbers (Knuth–Yao rolls) and cores that share scratch space to cut data hauls. Both speed up quick-guess math — the good-enough sums behind much of AI.
arxiv-2606-16248: Sky pros read the past by fitting sky math to sky facts — by hand math, by quick-guess math, or by full fake-sky runs. This paper lines up all three ways on late-era cosmos data and grades which to trust, when. A buyer's guide for cosmos fitters.
arxiv-2606-16548: Fractional quantum Hall states are among the most exotic phases of matter. This paper gives recipes for preparing them on quantum computers — step-by-step circuits that build these delicate states qubit by qubit. It targets quantum computing researchers who want to simulate topological matter on real hardware.
arxiv-2606-16648: Blocking sunlight with giant space shades is a proposed climate intervention, but getting a huge shade into orbit is the hard part. This paper presents a conceptual sunshade design with an origami-inspired folding strategy — packing a vast reflector into a rocket fairing. It targets space engineers studying solar geoengineering concepts.
arxiv-2606-16748: Computer-use agents click and type like humans — but do they adapt to YOUR machine? MyPCBench tests 'personally intelligent' computer-use agents: ones that learn your files, apps, and habits. It is for researchers building truly personal AI helpers. One bench, many desks.
